content.text:
Short answers: the project store's readers are mostly flexible already, but four exact-match version numbers would turn even safe changes into a lockout. On the server question, versioning the API is common and you already have it (`/ent/jusprin/v2/…`), but on its own it isn't enough. The bigger gap is that the server can't tell which JusPrin release is calling it. I read the code for both; nothing is changed or tested.

**1. Can the project store take foreseeable changes without breaking?**

What already copes well:
- The project document, which holds the chats, tool calls and print records, is kept as raw JSON and edited in place. If a newer build adds a field and an older build later edits the project, that field survives.
- Most fields are read with a default when missing: 188 reads use a default, and only 13 require the field.
- Version records are written once and never edited, and readers ignore fields they don't know.

How each likely change fares today:

| Change | Today |
|---|---|
| Add a field to a chat, tool call or print record | Fine, as long as nobody bumps a version number |
| Add a tool-call state (say "waiting") or source (say "printer") | An older build throws when it reads that chat ([ProjectStateDocument.cpp:58](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp:58), [:373](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp:373)) |
| Add a message state or print destination kind | An older build quietly misreads it: an unknown message state becomes "complete", and an unknown destination becomes "export" |
| Rename or remove a field | Breaks; version records require every field |
| Store part of the model somewhere new | An older build would ignore the new field and open an incomplete model without saying so |

The main blocker is that each of the four store files carries one number that means "the only format I accept". There's no way to say "older builds may read this" apart from "older builds must not read this". Git separates the two: its repository format version is paired with named extensions that older Git refuses only when it doesn't know them.

Proposal (not agreed):
- An additive change never bumps the number.
- A build refuses only a number higher than it knows, and says the project was made by a newer JusPrin.
- Older numbers get migrated.
- An unknown state or kind is read as "unknown" and shown plainly, instead of throwing or turning into a wrong value.

That covers everything in the table except the incomplete-model case. That one needs a real bump, so an older build refuses the project instead of opening a broken model.

**2. Is versioning the server API the common fix?**

It's part of it. Versioning covers changes that would break old apps, by running the old and new versions side by side. Most practitioner advice puts these first:
- Keep changes additive within a version.
- Know which client versions still call you.
- Publish how long old versions keep working.
- Have a way to tell an old app to update.

Two findings here:
- **The server can't see JusPrin's version.** Every chat, sign-in and account request goes through OrcaSlicer's HTTP class, which sends `User-Agent: JusPrin/2.5.0` ([Http.cpp:212](src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp:212)). That 2.5.0 is OrcaSlicer's version; JusPrin's own is 2.0.0 ([Version.hpp:14](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp:14)). Only the update check sends the real one. So the server can't count which JusPrin releases are still in use, or treat one differently.
- **The app has no "please update" response.** I found nothing that handles a reply meaning "this version is no longer supported". It has to be in the first release, because an app already installed can't learn it later.

Sources:
- [Capgo: API versioning strategy](https://capgo.app/blog/api-versioning-strategy/)
- [AppMaster: API versioning for mobile apps](https://appmaster.io/blog/api-versioning-mobile-apps)
- [Educative: API versioning](https://www.educative.io/courses/grokking-the-api-design-interview-crash-course/my9253DgPPn)
- [DEV: Old apps still call home](https://dev.to/goodbarber/old-apps-still-call-home-38mk)
- [Kordant API versioning plan](https://git.freno.me/Mike/Kordant/src/branch/master/tasks/web-production/28-api-versioning.md)

name: cmake-file-edit-forces-full-rebuild
description: "Editing sources.cmake, or adding a file to a globbed directory such as a new AgentUI skill, after a commit re-runs CMake, which bakes the new HEAD into -DGIT_COMMIT_HASH on every compile line, so ninja rebuilds all ~970 steps."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 62f57a5d-138a-485a-ac71-94d683a8c5db
  modified: 2026-11-01T13:16:25.404Z

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

2026-11-02 (connection-skill worktree): adding two new `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md` files did the same. The jusprin_web target globs that tree, so the build printed "GLOB mismatch!", re-ran CMake and started 945 steps for jusprin_web + agent_bridge_tests + shell_integration_harness.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake`, and new skill or other globbed files, before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

description: "Editing sources.cmake, or adding a file to a globbed directory such as a new AgentUI skill, after a commit re-runs CMake, which bakes the new HEAD into -DGIT_COMMIT_HASH on every compile line, so ninja rebuilds all ~970 steps."

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

2026-11-02 (connection-skill worktree): adding two new `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md` files did the same. The jusprin_web target globs that tree, so the build printed "GLOB mismatch!", re-ran CMake and started 945 steps for jusprin_web + agent_bridge_tests + shell_integration_harness.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake`, and new skill or other globbed files, before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

"""A stand-in JusPrin server that logs the method, path and User-Agent of every request."""
import json, sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

LOG = sys.argv[2]


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def record(self):
        with open(LOG, "a") as out:
            out.write(json.dumps({"method": self.command, "path": self.path,
                                  "userAgent": self.headers.get("User-Agent")}) + "\n")

    def reply(self, status, body, kind="application/json"):
        data = body.encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", kind)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def do_GET(self):
        self.record()
        if self.path.startswith("/ent/jusprin/v2/models"):
            self.reply(200, json.dumps({"data": [{"id": "slicer-1", "label": "Standard", "format": "responses"}]}))
        else:
            self.reply(200, "{}")

    def do_POST(self):
        self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0))
        self.record()
        if self.path.startswith("/ent/jusprin/v2/responses"):
            events = [{"type": "response.completed", "response": {"id": "r-1", "status": "completed", "output": [
                {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "ok"}]}]}}]
            self.reply(200, "".join(f"event: {e['type']}\ndata: {json.dumps(e)}\n\n" for e in events), "text/event-stream")
        else:
            self.reply(200, "{}")

    do_DELETE = do_GET

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), Handler).serve_forever()

content.text:
The build is still running; it needs to rebuild most of the app, which takes about an hour at 4 jobs. The stand-in server and the scratch data folder are ready, so the end-to-end check runs as soon as the build finishes. Meanwhile, here are answers to your three questions.

**Do we still need a versioned API once requests carry JusPrin's version?**

Yes, keep both. They do different jobs, and the versioned API already exists: every server path is under `/ent/jusprin/v2/`.
- The path version is how you make a breaking change. You'd run `/v3/` next to `/v2/`, so installed apps keep using `/v2/` untouched.
- The version in each request tells you who is still on `/v2/`. Without it you can't know when it's safe to switch `/v2/` off, or treat a release with a known bug differently.

So nothing more needs versioning now. The missing piece is the one I mentioned earlier: a server reply the app understands as "this version is no longer supported, please update". It has to ship in the first release to be usable later.

**Do the two lists of project-store proposals overlap?**

Yes. They're the same plan, described once as rules for the format and once as the work to build it. Merged, it's five items:
1. An additive change never bumps the format number. This is only in the first list.
2. A build refuses a number higher than it knows and says the project was made by a newer JusPrin. This is in both lists.
3. Older numbers get migrated, step by step. This is in both lists.
4. A state or kind the build doesn't know is read as "unknown". This is only in the first list.
5. A project store saved by each release is committed as a test file, and a test checks that the next build opens it. This is only in the second list.

**Is there any reason not to do them?**

No reason not to, but each one has a cost:
- **Item 1 needs a judgment on every change.** The question each time is whether an older build, ignoring the new field, would do something wrong. If the answer is yes, the change must bump the number. The case that must bump is a newer build storing part of the model somewhere new, because an older build would open an incomplete model.
- **Item 2 means going back a version locks you out.** Someone who installs an older JusPrin can't open projects saved by a newer one after a bump. That's on purpose, because the alternative is quietly losing data.
- **Item 4 is about showing, not acting.** An older build may display "unknown" for a newer state, but must not act on it, for example by treating an unknown tool-call state as finished. Each place that shows these values needs a plain "unknown" display.
- **Items 3 and 5 add a release step.** Every bump needs a migration and its test kept forever, and every release needs its saved store committed as a test file.
- **Timing matters.** Before the first release this is cheapest, because nothing has to be migrated yet. After it, the first release's format is something you'll have to migrate from.

# Before you start: read the dev docs

Before doing any dev work in this project, read the root `README.md` and `obico-server/CONTRIBUTING.md`. They document the dev process that is NOT obvious from the code and that you are expected to follow, including:

- **Dependencies:** declare packages in `obico-server/backend/Pipfile` and regenerate `requirements.txt` with pipenv. Do NOT edit `requirements.txt` directly.
- **Pull requests:** open PRs against obico-server's `master` branch, not `release`.
- **i18n:** a UI change that adds or edits a `$t('...')` string is not complete until all frontend locale files (`obico-server/frontend/src/i18n/locales/`) are synced. See the README's "Frontend i18n" section.

# Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

# Start backend and frontend dev servers

This project uses Docker Compose. The backend Django server runs inside the "web" Docker container. you can start the backend Django servers by running `docker compose up -d`

** Do not forget to prefix all python commands with `docker compose exec web xxx`.***

The frontend server runs on the host. Use this command to start a Vue dev server:

1. Load nvm first:

```
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"  # This loads nvm
```

2. Now you can start Vue dev server:

`cd web_ent/frontend && nvm use && npm ci && VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd) npm run serve`

**Important**: `VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd)` is required because `package.json` is a symlink to `../../obico-server/frontend/package.json`. Without it, vue-cli-service can load the wrong `vue.config.js` and write `webpack-stats.json` to the wrong location.

The dev server supports hot module replacement, so you don't need to rebuild after changing Vue files - changes are automatically detected and reloaded in the browser.

For anything related to Docker that you are not sure, check docker-compose.yaml and docker-compose.override.yaml to understand. if you are still not sure, stop and ask me.

# Pager on terminal

I use less as the default pager for Git commands (like git log, git diff, etc.). When generating Git commands, please always include the appropriate option to disable the pager, such as:
	•	--no-pager (e.g., git --no-pager log)
	•	or setting GIT_PAGER=cat (e.g., GIT_PAGER=cat git diff)

This ensures the output goes directly to the terminal without invoking a pager like less.

# Git structure

The top-level Git repo `tsd-enterprise` includes the public, open-source `obico-server` repo as a Git submodule. The dependency is strictly one-way: `tsd-enterprise` depends on `obico-server`; `obico-server` must not depend on or have knowledge of `tsd-enterprise`.

`obico-server` must remain able to run on its own. Hobbyists use it to run self-hosted servers without access to `tsd-enterprise`, its code, configuration, secrets, or private infrastructure.

Before making any change in `obico-server`:

- Decide whether the change belongs in `obico-server` or `tsd-enterprise`. Put enterprise-specific behavior and integrations in `tsd-enterprise`. Add shared functionality or extension points to `obico-server` only when they belong in the standalone project and preserve the one-way dependency.

from django.urls import path

from . import sign_in, views, web
from .gateway import GatewayEndpoint

# BEFORE PRODUCTION: JusPrin may get a domain of its own instead of
# app.obico.io. These endpoints, the OAuth sign-in pages the desktop app opens
# (/o/authorize/ and the two pages below), their TLS certificate and ingress
# rules, and the desktop app's default gateway address all move with that
# decision; see the rollout notes in the ops repo.
urlpatterns = [
    path('models', views.models, name='jusprin_v2_models'),
    path('account', views.account, name='jusprin_v2_account'),
    path('account_box', views.account_box, name='jusprin_v2_account_box'),
    path('print_reports', views.print_reports, name='jusprin_v2_print_reports'),
    # The server's pages the app opens in its sheet; see views.web_link.
    path('web_link', views.web_link, name='jusprin_v2_web_link'),
    path('web/open/<str:token>', views.web_open, name='jusprin_v2_web_open'),
    path('web/done', views.web_done, name='jusprin_v2_web_done'),
    path('web/prices', web.prices, name='jusprin_v2_web_prices'),
    path('web/billing', web.billing_page, name='jusprin_v2_web_billing'),
    path('web/checkout', web.checkout, name='jusprin_v2_web_checkout'),
    path('web/checkout/done', web.checkout_done, name='jusprin_v2_web_checkout_done'),
    path('web/cancel', web.cancel, name='jusprin_v2_web_cancel'),
    path('web/portal', web.portal, name='jusprin_v2_web_portal'),
    # Served by jusprin.v2.asgi, not by Django's request handling; see gateway.py.
    path('messages', GatewayEndpoint('anthropic'), name='jusprin_v2_messages'),
    path('responses', GatewayEndpoint('responses'), name='jusprin_v2_responses'),
    path('signed_in/', views.signed_in, name='jusprin_v2_signed_in'),
    path('sign_in_failed/', views.sign_in_failed, name='jusprin_v2_sign_in_failed'),
    # Signing in by email from inside the app: allauth's API for apps, the
    # views the app uses and no others; see sign_in.py.
    path('auth/code/request', sign_in.request_code, name='jusprin_v2_auth_code_request'),
    path('auth/code/confirm', sign_in.confirm_code, name='jusprin_v2_auth_code_confirm'),
    path('auth/login', sign_in.login, name='jusprin_v2_auth_login'),
]
"""The gateway's own error answers.

Every error the gateway returns has the body
{"type": "error", "error": {"code": <code>, "message": <message>}} with text
from this table, never bytes from upstream. The client treats 401 as "signed
out", so 401 means only that the person's own token was missing or rejected.
credits_exhausted adds what the client needs to offer a way on, beside "error".
"""
import json

MESSAGES = {
    'invalid_request': 'The request is not valid.',
    'unknown_model': 'This model is not available.',
    'method_not_allowed': 'This method is not allowed here.',
    'unauthorized': 'Sign in to JusPrin to continue.',
    'quota_exhausted': 'Your JusPrin AI credits for this period are used up.',
    'credits_exhausted': 'You do not have enough credits for this message.',
    'text_too_short': 'A report needs a few sentences.',
    'photo_needed': 'A report needs a photo of the printed object.',
    'photo_unreadable': 'That photo could not be read.',
    'already_reported': 'This print already has a report.',
    'request_too_large': 'The request is too large.',
    'rate_limited': 'Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.',
    'upstream_error': 'The model service could not answer.',
    'unavailable': 'The model service is unavailable. Try again shortly.',
    'timeout': 'The model service took too long to answer.',
    'busy': 'JusPrin is busy right now. Try again in a moment.',
}


class GatewayError(Exception):
    """An answer the gateway gives instead of forwarding. Raised inside one
    request and turned into a response at the endpoint boundary only."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str = None, details: dict = None):
        super().__init__(code)
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = message or MESSAGES[code]
        self.details = details

    def body(self) -> bytes:
        return error_body(self.code, self.message, self.details)


def error_body(code: str, message: str = None, details: dict = None) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps({'type': 'error', 'error': {'code': code, 'message': message or MESSAGES[code]},
                       **(details or {})}).encode()


def credits_exhausted(cost: int, balance: int, details: dict) -> GatewayError:
    unit = 'credit' if cost == 1 else 'credits'
    return GatewayError(402, 'credits_exhausted', f'This message needs {cost} {unit}; you have {balance}.', details)
from oauth2_provider.oauth2_backends import get_oauthlib_core


def authenticate(request):
    """The active user whose OAuth2 bearer token the request carries, or None.

    The same check DRF's OAuth2Authentication runs for the v1 JusPrin views: any
    valid token of the provider, whichever application issued it, no scope
    required. A deactivated account's token is refused as well.
    """
    valid, oauthlib_request = get_oauthlib_core().verify_request(request, scopes=[])
    if not valid or not oauthlib_request.user.is_active:
        return None
    return oauthlib_request.user

class GatewayEndpoint:
    # Bearer-token requests carry no CSRF token. Without this, a request that
    # reaches Django's request handling gets CsrfViewMiddleware's 403 instead
    # of the ImproperlyConfigured below, and never reaches Sentry.
    csrf_exempt = True

    def __init__(self, fmt: str):
        self.fmt = fmt

    def __call__(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        # Django only reaches this when the process does not serve
        # jusprin.v2.asgi (a WSGI worker, or a different ASGI_APPLICATION). A
        # deployment fault: let it reach Sentry rather than stream badly.
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(
            f'{request.path} must be served by the jusprin.v2.asgi application; '
            'it cannot stream from a Django view in this Django version')

    async def asgi(self, scope, receive, send):
        # Neither daphne nor channels opens a ThreadSensitiveContext, so without
        # this one every sync_to_async call below would run on asgiref's single
        # thread per process, behind every websocket consumer's database work.
        # Django's own ASGI handler opens one per request in the same way.
        async with ThreadSensitiveContext():
            # Django's own handler brackets every request with these signals;
            # they are what closes stale database connections.
            await sync_to_async(signals.request_started.send, thread_sensitive=True)(
                sender=self.__class__, scope=scope)
            try:
                await self._handle(scope, receive, send)
            finally:
                await sync_to_async(_finish_request, thread_sensitive=True)(self.__class__)

    async def _handle(self, scope, receive, send):
        async with contextlib.AsyncExitStack() as stack:
            await self._handle_in(scope, receive, send, stack)

    async def _handle_in(self, scope, receive, send, stack):
        try:
            if scope['method'] != 'POST':
                raise GatewayError(405, 'method_not_allowed')
            user = await sync_to_async(_authenticate_scope, thread_sensitive=True)(scope)
            if user is None:
                raise GatewayError(401, 'unauthorized')
            headers = _headers(scope)
            turn_id = headers.get('x-jusprin-turn', '')
            request_kind = headers.get('x-jusprin-request', '')
            chat_id = headers.get('x-jusprin-chat')
            if not TURN_ID.match(turn_id):
                raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The X-JusPrin-Turn header is missing or not valid.')
            if request_kind not in REQUEST_KINDS:
                raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The X-JusPrin-Request header must be reply, title or note.')
            if chat_id is not None and not capture.CHAT_ID.match(chat_id):
                raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The X-JusPrin-Chat header must be 32 lowercase hex digits.')
            large = await stack.enter_async_context(_large_request_slot(scope))
            raw_body = await _read_body(receive, settings.JUSPRIN_V2_MAX_BODY_BYTES)
            if raw_body is None:
                return  # the client left before sending the whole body
            if large or len(raw_body) > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_LARGE_BODY_BYTES:
                # Parsing and re-encoding megabytes of JSON takes long enough
                # to stall every websocket this process serves.

class GatewayEndpoint:
    # Bearer-token requests carry no CSRF token. Without this, a request that
    # reaches Django's request handling gets CsrfViewMiddleware's 403 instead
    # of the ImproperlyConfigured below, and never reaches Sentry.
    csrf_exempt = True

    def __init__(self, fmt: str):
        self.fmt = fmt

    def __call__(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        # Django only reaches this when the process does not serve
        # jusprin.v2.asgi (a WSGI worker, or a different ASGI_APPLICATION). A
        # deployment fault: let it reach Sentry rather than stream badly.
        raise ImproperlyConfigured(
            f'{request.path} must be served by the jusprin.v2.asgi application; '
            'it cannot stream from a Django view in this Django version')

    async def asgi(self, scope, receive, send):
        # Neither daphne nor channels opens a ThreadSensitiveContext, so without
        # this one every sync_to_async call below would run on asgiref's single
        # thread per process, behind every websocket consumer's database work.
        # Django's own ASGI handler opens one per request in the same way.
        async with ThreadSensitiveContext():
            # Django's own handler brackets every request with these signals;
            # they are what closes stale database connections.
            await sync_to_async(signals.request_started.send, thread_sensitive=True)(
                sender=self.__class__, scope=scope)
            try:
                await self._handle(scope, receive, send)
            finally:
                await sync_to_async(_finish_request, thread_sensitive=True)(self.__class__)

    async def _handle(self, scope, receive, send):
        async with contextlib.AsyncExitStack() as stack:
            await self._handle_in(scope, receive, send, stack)

    async def _handle_in(self, scope, receive, send, stack):
        try:
            if scope['method'] != 'POST':
                raise GatewayError(405, 'method_not_allowed')
            user = await sync_to_async(_authenticate_scope, thread_sensitive=True)(scope)
            if user is None:
                raise GatewayError(401, 'unauthorized')

            turn_id = headers.get('x-jusprin-turn', '')
            request_kind = headers.get('x-jusprin-request', '')
            chat_id = headers.get('x-jusprin-chat')
            if not TURN_ID.match(turn_id):
                raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The X-JusPrin-Turn header is missing or not valid.')

"""POST /ent/jusprin/v2/web_link and the link it answers: a server page opened
signed in as the app's account, once; and the done address the pages end at."""
import json
import uuid
from datetime import timedelta

from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from django.core.cache import cache
from django.test import Client, TestCase, override_settings
from django.utils import timezone
from oauth2_provider.models import AccessToken, Application

from app.models import Syndicate, User

URL = '/ent/jusprin/v2/web_link'


class WebLinkTests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        # The pages are drawn in the host's syndicate's brand.
        base, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=1, defaults={'name': 'base'})
        base.sites.add(Site.objects.get_or_create(domain='testserver', defaults={'name': 'testserver'})[0])
        Site.objects.clear_cache()
        # The cached site would outlive this test's rolled-back rows.
        self.addCleanup(Site.objects.clear_cache)
        self.user = User.objects.create(email=f'link-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com')
        app = Application.objects.create(
            client_id=f'JusPrin2-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}', name='JusPrin 2', client_type=Application.CLIENT_PUBLIC,
            authorization_grant_type=Application.GRANT_AUTHORIZATION_CODE, redirect_uris='http://127.0.0.1/callback')
        self.token = AccessToken.objects.create(user=self.user, application=app, token=uuid.uuid4().hex,
                                                scope='read write', expires=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)).token

    def ask(self, body, token=None):
        return Client().post(URL, json.dumps(body), content_type='application/json',
                             HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {token or self.token}')

    def link(self, body):
        response = self.ask(body)
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response['Cache-Control']), (200, 'no-store'))
        return response.json()['url']

    def test_a_wrong_token_is_refused(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ask({'page': 'prices'}, token='not-a-token').status_code, 401)

    def test_with_no_token_it_is_credits_and_plans_as_a_guest(self):
        for page in ('prices', 'billing'):
            response = Client().post(URL, json.dumps({'page': page, 'from': 'welcome'}), content_type='application/json')
            self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response['Cache-Control']), (200, 'no-store'))
            self.assertEqual(response.json()['url'], 'http://testserver/ent/jusprin/v2/web/prices?guest=1&from=welcome')
        response = Client().post(URL, '{}', content_type='application/json')
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['url'], 'http://testserver/ent/jusprin/v2/web/prices?guest=1')

    def test_a_body_that_is_not_an_object_is_refused(self):
        self.assertEqual(Client().post(URL, 'nope', content_type='application/json',
                                       HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {self.token}').status_code, 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.ask(['prices']).status_code, 400)

    def test_the_link_signs_in_and_goes_to_the_page_with_where_the_click_was(self):
        url = self.link({'page': 'billing', 'from': 'account'})
        self.assertTrue(url.startswith('http://testserver/ent/jusprin/v2/web/open/'))

"""POST /ent/jusprin/v2/web_link and the link it answers: a server page opened
signed in as the app's account, once; and the done address the pages end at."""
import json
import uuid
from datetime import timedelta

from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from django.core.cache import cache
from django.test import Client, TestCase, override_settings
from django.utils import timezone
from oauth2_provider.models import AccessToken, Application

from app.models import Syndicate, User

URL = '/ent/jusprin/v2/web_link'


class WebLinkTests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        # The pages are drawn in the host's syndicate's brand.
        base, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=1, defaults={'name': 'base'})
        base.sites.add(Site.objects.get_or_create(domain='testserver', defaults={'name': 'testserver'})[0])
        Site.objects.clear_cache()
        # The cached site would outlive this test's rolled-back rows.
        self.addCleanup(Site.objects.clear_cache)
        self.user = User.objects.create(email=f'link-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com')
        app = Application.objects.create(
            client_id=f'JusPrin2-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}', name='JusPrin 2', client_type=Application.CLIENT_PUBLIC,
            authorization_grant_type=Application.GRANT_AUTHORIZATION_CODE, redirect_uris='http://127.0.0.1/callback')
        self.token = AccessToken.objects.create(user=self.user, application=app, token=uuid.uuid4().hex,
                                                scope='read write', expires=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)).token

    def ask(self, body, token=None):
        return Client().post(URL, json.dumps(body), content_type='application/json',
                             HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {token or self.token}')

    def link(self, body):
        response = self.ask(body)
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response['Cache-Control']), (200, 'no-store'))
        return response.json()['url']

    def test_a_wrong_token_is_refused(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ask({'page': 'prices'}, token='not-a-token').status_code, 401)

    def test_with_no_token_it_is_credits_and_plans_as_a_guest(self):
        for page in ('prices', 'billing'):
            response = Client().post(URL, json.dumps({'page': page, 'from': 'welcome'}), content_type='application/json')
            self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response['Cache-Control']), (200, 'no-store'))
            self.assertEqual(response.json()['url'], 'http://testserver/ent/jusprin/v2/web/prices?guest=1&from=welcome')
        response = Client().post(URL, '{}', content_type='application/json')
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['url'], 'http://testserver/ent/jusprin/v2/web/prices?guest=1')

    def test_a_body_that_is_not_an_object_is_refused(self):
        self.assertEqual(Client().post(URL, 'nope', content_type='application/json',
                                       HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {self.token}').status_code, 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.ask(['prices']).status_code, 400)

    def test_the_link_signs_in_and_goes_to_the_page_with_where_the_click_was(self):
        url = self.link({'page': 'billing', 'from': 'account'})
        self.assertTrue(url.startswith('http://testserver/ent/jusprin/v2/web/open/'))

        signals.request_started.disconnect(close_old_connections)
        signals.request_finished.disconnect(close_old_connections)
        self.addCleanup(signals.request_started.connect, close_old_connections)
        self.addCleanup(signals.request_finished.connect, close_old_connections)
        # The gateway also calls it itself, for the same reason.
        patch_attr(self, gateway, 'close_old_connections', lambda: None)

        prefix = patch_attr(self, credits, 'KEY_PREFIX', f'jusprin:v2:test:{uuid.uuid4().hex}')
        self.addCleanup(lambda: [credits.REDIS.delete(k) for k in credits.REDIS.scan_iter(prefix + ':*')])
        self.user = User.objects.create(email=f'gw-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com')
        app = Application.objects.create(

            authorization_grant_type=Application.GRANT_AUTHORIZATION_CODE, redirect_uris='http://127.0.0.1/callback')

        patch_attr(self, gateway, 'upstream_client', lambda: self.upstream.client())

"""The gateway's own error answers.

Every error the gateway returns has the body
{"type": "error", "error": {"code": <code>, "message": <message>}} with text
from this table, never bytes from upstream. The client treats 401 as "signed
out", so 401 means only that the person's own token was missing or rejected.
credits_exhausted adds what the client needs to offer a way on, beside "error".
"""
import json

MESSAGES = {
    'invalid_request': 'The request is not valid.',
    'unknown_model': 'This model is not available.',
    'method_not_allowed': 'This method is not allowed here.',
    'unauthorized': 'Sign in to JusPrin to continue.',
    'quota_exhausted': 'Your JusPrin AI credits for this period are used up.',
    'credits_exhausted': 'You do not have enough credits for this message.',
    'text_too_short': 'A report needs a few sentences.',
    'photo_needed': 'A report needs a photo of the printed object.',
    'photo_unreadable': 'That photo could not be read.',
    'already_reported': 'This print already has a report.',
    'request_too_large': 'The request is too large.',
    'rate_limited': 'Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.',
    'upstream_error': 'The model service could not answer.',
    'unavailable': 'The model service is unavailable. Try again shortly.',
    'timeout': 'The model service took too long to answer.',
    'busy': 'JusPrin is busy right now. Try again in a moment.',
}


class GatewayError(Exception):
    """An answer the gateway gives instead of forwarding. Raised inside one
    request and turned into a response at the endpoint boundary only."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str = None, details: dict = None):
        super().__init__(code)
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = message or MESSAGES[code]
        self.details = details

    def body(self) -> bytes:
        return error_body(self.code, self.message, self.details)


def error_body(code: str, message: str = None, details: dict = None) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps({'type': 'error', 'error': {'code': code, 'message': message or MESSAGES[code]},
                       **(details or {})}).encode()


def credits_exhausted(cost: int, balance: int, details: dict) -> GatewayError:
    unit = 'credit' if cost == 1 else 'credits'
    return GatewayError(402, 'credits_exhausted', f'This message needs {cost} {unit}; you have {balance}.', details)

        super().__init__(code)
        self.status = status
        self.code = code
        self.message = message or MESSAGES[code]
        self.details = details

    def body(self) -> bytes:
        return error_body(self.code, self.message, self.details)


def error_body(code: str, message: str = None, details: dict = None) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps({'type': 'error', 'error': {'code': code, 'message': message or MESSAGES[code]},
                       **(details or {})}).encode()


def credits_exhausted(cost: int, balance: int, details: dict) -> GatewayError:
    unit = 'credit' if cost == 1 else 'credits'
    return GatewayError(402, 'credits_exhausted', f'This message needs {cost} {unit}; you have {balance}.', details)

name: workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac
description: "On macOS the workspace adapter harness never reaches GUI_App::post_init; closing its frame crashes, so it exits via ExitMainLoop unless post_initialized()"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ed4bbcf2-a467-44f4-bceb-b20f93cd25d8
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:28:53.409Z
---

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake); Moonraker and OctoPrint: `tests/printer_hosts/README.md` (Docker). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake); Moonraker and OctoPrint: `tests/printer_hosts/README.md` (Docker). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

1	#pragma once

3	// The rule every file of the local project store follows for the format
4	// number it carries:
5	//  - A change that a build without it still reads correctly, such as a new
6	//    field or a new list, keeps the number. Such a build keeps what it does
7	//    not know when it edits the file in place.
8	//  - A change that such a build would misread raises the number, and adds a
9	//    step to the file's list that brings a file of the previous number to it.
10	//    So does storing part of the model somewhere new: a build that ignored it
11	//    would open an incomplete model.
12	//  - A build reads every number from the file's first to its own, upgrading
13	//    an older file step by step as it reads it, and refuses a higher one: a
14	//    newer JusPrin wrote it, and reading it could lose what it holds.
15	
16	#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
17	
18	#include <functional>
19	#include <stdexcept>
20	#include <string>
21	#include <vector>

23	namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Workspace {

25	// A stored file with a format number above this build's own.
26	class NewerFormatError : public std::runtime_error
27	{
28	public:
29	    using std::runtime_error::runtime_error;
30	};
31	
32	struct StoredFormat
33	{
34	    enum class Check { Readable, Newer, Unreadable };
35	
36	    std::string key;   // the member that holds the number
37	    int         first; // the oldest number this build reads
38	    // steps[i] brings a file of number first + i to first + i + 1.
39	    std::vector<std::function<void(nlohmann::json&)>> steps;
40	
41	    int current() const { return first + int(steps.size()); }
42	
43	    // Brings `value` to current() in place. Newer for a number above it;
44	    // Unreadable, with `value` untouched, for a missing number or one below first.
45	    Check upgrade(nlohmann::json& value) const
46	    {
47	        if (!value.is_object() || !value.contains(key) || !value[key].is_number_integer())
48	            return Check::Unreadable;
49	        const int number = value[key].get<int>();
50	        if (number > current())
51	            return Check::Newer;
52	        if (number < first)
53	            return Check::Unreadable;
54	        for (int at = number; at < current(); ++at) {
55	            steps[std::size_t(at - first)](value);
56	            value[key] = at + 1;
57	        }
58	        return Check::Readable;
59	    }
60	};
61	
62	} // namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Workspace
